title: feat: declare endpoint-agent input and output modalities
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Adds optional input/output modality declarations through the existing endpoint-agent create, update and account-list APIs.
- Reuses the same modality arrays and enums as text models, including multiple outputs and 3D; publishes them in /models and /v1/models.
- Preserves declarations during unrelated edits and keeps unconfigured agents text-only. Routing, billing and prompt-agent inheritance are unchanged.
- No new endpoints, migration, manual SQL or model-specific rules. Shared schemas provide the API documentation.
- Validation: 154 local tests, Gen and Enter TypeScript checks, and Biome passed. The local Enter build wrapper hit a brand-asset copy error; direct TypeScript passed.

Addresses #14162.

gist.headline: Agents declare their senses
gist.blurb: Endpoint agents can now say what they take in and what they make, from text to multiple outputs and 3D. The hive’s model catalog gets a little more honest about its capabilities.
gist.summary: Endpoint-agent create, update, and account-list APIs now support optional shared input/output modality declarations—including multiple output modalities and 3D—and publish them through /models and /v1/models.
gist.impact: Developers can discover each endpoint agent’s declared media capabilities in the standard model listings, while unconfigured agents remain text-only and existing routing, billing, and prompt-agent inheritance stay the same.
gist.visual_concept: Polli, wearing tiny librarian glasses, updates a cozy garden catalog beside a CRT monitor robot. The catalog shows small pixel symbols for text, image, audio, video, and a tiny 3D cube growing from labeled code-plants, representing agents accurately declaring their inputs and multiple outputs.
